Report_ID: Neck pain intensity (VAS) at 8 weeks (end of study)
Title: Effectiveness of an application-based neck exercise as a pain management tool for office workers with chronic neck pain and functional disability: A pilot randomized trial
Author: Lee, JaeHyuk; Lee, MinYoung; Lim, TaeHyun; Kim, TaeYeong; Kim, SeungMin; Suh, DongWon; Lee, SangHeon; Yoon, BumChul
Comment: M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (3.69 − 2.73 = 0.96) from explicitly reported 8-week post-intervention means in a simple two-group between-subjects design; positive value favours the app group (less pain). The reported P = 0.02 comes from a Mann-Whitney U test on pre-post change (improvement) scores, not on post-intervention means; no effect size, CI, or test statistic is reported. Groups differed at baseline (app 5.20 vs control 4.02). Outcome scale min/max left empty because the paper's stated 0–100 mm range contradicts the 0–10-scale values in Table 2. Very small pilot sample.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('App-based neck exercise group (smartphone app-delivered McKenzie neck exercise, 10–15 min/day, 2 days/week, 8 weeks)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: telerehabilitation / musculoskeletal pain management (chronic neck pain in office workers)
Medium: smartphone application (mobile app) with weekly text messages
Content length: 8 weeks intervention; assessments at baseline and 8 weeks
Participant type: office workers with chronic neck pain (>6 months), aged 25–35 years, >6 h/day computer use
Recruitment source: Office workers at Korea University Graduate School, South Korea
Outcome measurement: Post-intervention (8-week) VAS mean (SD) per group; between-group comparison of pre-post improvement by Mann-Whitney U test
Outcome variable: Neck pain intensity (VAS) at 8 weeks (end of study)
outcome_units: VAS score (paper states VAS recorded in millimeters on a 0–100 mm line, but Table 2 values are on a 0–10 scale)

Report_ID: Neck pain intensity (VAS) change score (ΔPain Intensity), 8 weeks
Title: Effect of a stress management program on subjects with neck pain: A pilot randomized controlled trial
Author: Metikaridis, Hadjipavlou, Artemiadis, Chrousos, Darviri
Comment: M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean = -0.72 − (-2.4) = 1.68 VAS points (positive favours the intervention, i.e. greater pain reduction); both change-score means are explicitly reported for a simple two-arm between-subjects design. SE_diff computed from the reported SDs and Ns: sqrt(1.93²/28 + 1.70²/25) = 0.499; not reported by the paper. The paper's own between-group test was a non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test with only a p-value reported (no U statistic, no effect size). CONSTRUCT-MATCH CAVEAT: the intervention is a home-practised stress management/relaxation program delivered via audio CD with weekly in-person clinic visits and counselling — it is not clearly "telerehabilitation delivering exercise or physical activity"; the comparator is a genuine no-active-care control. Reported direction (greater reduction in IG) is consistent with the reported numbers.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention group: 8-week home-practised stress management/relaxation program via audio CD (diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation; autogenic training and guided imagery added at sessions 4 and 6), weekly clinic visits and lifestyle/stress counselling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: primary care clinic with home practice
Participant type: Adults (18–75 years, predominantly middle-aged women) with chronic non-specific neck pain recruited from municipal primary care clinics in Athens
Recruitment source: Municipal Clinics of Cholargos-Papagos, Agia Paraskevi and Halandri, Athens, Greece
Outcome measurement: Change from baseline to 8 weeks in VAS neck pain intensity (mean ± SD), compared between groups with Mann-Whitney U test
Outcome variable: Neck pain intensity (VAS) change score (ΔPain Intensity), 8 weeks

Title: The effectiveness of telerehabilitation-based structured exercise therapy for chronic nonspecific neck pain: A randomized controlled trial
Author: Özel M, Kaya Ciddi P
Comment: SDs are not reported; only means with 95% CIs (SD can be derived from the CI half-width and n=22 downstream). The p<0.001 stated in the text accompanies the three-group post-therapy comparison (omnibus ANOVA), so it was NOT recorded as the pairwise p-value; the paper's own pairwise evidence for RSG vs CG is only the Table 2 superscript "b" indicating p<0.05. Baseline NPRS differed significantly between arms (RSG 6.77 vs CG 5.55, p=0.001), so post-therapy means are subject to baseline imbalance.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Remote supervised telerehabilitation group (RSG) - structured exercise therapy with Zoom videoconference supervision') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
domain: musculoskeletal rehabilitation / telerehabilitation - chronic nonspecific neck pain
Medium: telerehabilitation (e-mailed exercise videos/brochures plus synchronous Zoom videoconference and text messaging)
Participant type: adults (≥18 years) with chronic nonspecific neck pain of at least 3 months' duration
Recruitment source: Volunteers responding to study announcements on social media and WhatsApp groups, physician-referred for rehabilitation
Outcome measurement: Group mean NPRS score at post-therapy (week 4) with 95% CI

Report_ID: Pain intensity on movement (VAS motion) at 6 weeks post-randomisation
Title: Effects of Interactive Telerehabilitation Practices in Office Workers with Chronic Nonspecific Neck Pain: Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Özlü, Ünver, Tuna, Erdoğan
Comment: No means or SDs are reported anywhere in the paper — only medians with IQRs — so Hedges g / M_diff / SE_diff cannot be validly computed and were left empty. The only between-group inferential statistic is an omnibus Kruskal–Wallis test across all three arms (post p<0.001), which the synthesis plan excludes; no isolated Group 1 vs Group 3 test statistic or p-value is reported, so p_value was left empty. Direction of effect (Group 1 lower pain than Group 3) is consistent with both the reported medians and the paper's own pairwise notation '1<2=3'. Table 2 in the source text is layout-garbled (group labels shifted into the PRE column); values were assigned to groups by row order. Per-group n=40 from Methods/flowchart (final analysed N).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1 – interactive telerehabilitation exercise program + office ergonomics training') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); mean/SD estimated from median/IQR via Wan et al. (2014): treatment mean=5.2500 SD=0.7689, control mean=7.3125 SD=1.3456 -- APPROXIMATION, not directly reported
domain: telerehabilitation / musculoskeletal physiotherapy (chronic nonspecific neck pain)
Topic of Content: Neck exercise program: warm-up/stretching, cervical isometric strengthening, motor control (craniocervical) and posture correction exercises
Participant type: Office workers aged 24–45 years with chronic nonspecific neck pain, working >35 h/week at a desk
Recruitment source: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation outpatient clinics, Kutahya Health Sciences University
Outcome measurement: Median [IQR] post-treatment VAS score per group
Outcome variable: Pain intensity on movement (VAS motion) at 6 weeks post-randomisation

Report_ID: Mean neck pain intensity during first 3 months (daily NRS)
Title: App-Based Relaxation Exercises for Patients With Chronic Neck Pain: Pragmatic Randomized Trial
Author: Pach D, Blödt S, Wang J, Keller T, Bergmann B, Rogge AA, Barth J, Icke K, Roll S, Witt CM
Comment: Only adjusted means with 95% CIs are reported; no SDs are given, so Hedges g cannot be computed from means+SDs. M_diff (0.3) is the paper's own reported difference signed as INTERVENTION MINUS CONTROL, i.e. a positive value indicates MORE pain in the app group (favours control); the sign must be flipped to match the plan's convention that positive favours telerehabilitation. SE_diff was derived as (0.7 - (-0.2))/3.92 = 0.230 from the reported 95% CI of the group difference. Per-group analysed Ns are not explicitly stated for Table 2 (full analysis set, no imputation); randomised Ns of 110 per group were used.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('App-based relaxation intervention plus usual care') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Design Type: pragmatic randomized controlled trial, 2-arm parallel group, 1:1
domain: mHealth / chronic neck pain / mind-body relaxation
Medium: smartphone app (Relaxneck; iOS and Android), audio relaxation exercises
Participant type: Adults aged 18-65 years with chronic (>12 weeks) neck pain and previous week's average neck pain intensity >=4 on NRS, smartphone owners
Recruitment source: Brochures/posters in universities, gyms, and general practitioners' offices, plus subway advertising; single center in Berlin, Germany
Outcome measurement: Numeric Rating Scale, 0-10, mean of daily measurements over first 3 months (primary endpoint)
Outcome variable: Mean neck pain intensity during first 3 months (daily NRS)
